title: Microsoft Teams: Workflows template adds tag members to channels automatically
summary: Hold: the data-policy PowerShell call asks for a policy name, but Microsoft's reference requires its identifier. The optional behaviour, rollout dates and other controls are supported; the flow-ownership checklist also names a control missing from the table.

claims.claim: Microsoft is introducing the Workflows template Join member to channel when user is added to tag.
claims.quote: We are introducing the Join member to channel when user is added to tag template in the Workflows app

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Once configured, the workflow automatically adds a user to selected channels whenever that user is added to the associated team tag.
claims.quote: Once configured, the workflow runs whenever a user is added to the tag, eliminating the need to add members to each channel manually.

claims.claim: Team owners can choose to configure the workflow.
claims.quote: Team owners can configure the workflow at any time if desired.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationales
claims.claim: The template is user-opt-in: nothing changes by default and it does not run until someone in a team configures it.
claims.quote: Nothing changes by default. The template is optional and does not run until someone in a team configures it.

claims.claim: Microsoft requires no administrator action for this change.
claims.quote: No action is required.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes the template as useful for location-based or project-based groups whose tags correspond to sites, regions or projects.
claims.quote: This is especially useful for location-based or project-based groups where tags correspond to specific sites, regions, or projects

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The notice says the template applies to standard channels and shared channels shared with everyone on the team.
claims.quote: This applies to channels that all team members can access by default: standard channels and shared channels that are shared with everyone on the team.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this specific template.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Workflows Join member to channel when user is added to tag template licence connectors account tenant disable switch removal; exact template name with license/connectors. Read Create flows in Microsoft Teams and Install the Workflows app; no template-specific description.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The notice identifies Microsoft Teams, the Workflows app and Power Automate as the services involved.
claims.quote:
Platforms and services
- Microsoft Teams- Workflows app- Power Automate

claims.claim: The Workflows app creates Power Automate cloud flows from templates.
claims.quote: Workflows app: You can use the Workflows app to create flows from a template or from scratch.

claims.where: controls[3]; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant UI or automation switch for this template alone is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Join member to channel template disable admin PowerShell Graph policy. Read manage-apps, Set-CsTeamsTargetingPolicy and Update-M365TeamsApp; search excerpts cover team-creation templates and membership APIs, not a switch for this Workflows template.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether this template can target other channel types.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams user is added to tag workflow connection account removal private channels. Read MC1540351, Create flows in Microsoft Teams and private/shared channel search excerpts; the notice names supported types but none describes targeting other types with this template.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Flows created within the Workflows app reside in the organisation's default environment.
claims.quote: When you create flows from within the Workflows app in Microsoft Teams, they're always created in your organization's default environment.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A data policy covering the default environment governs connector use by flows created there.
claims.quote: Facebook and Twitter connectors are altogether blocked from being used in any app or flow in non-test environments such as production or default environments.

claims.where: licensing.notes; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The connector list for this specific template is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: exact Join member to channel when user is added to tag template name with license/connectors. Read Create flows in Microsoft Teams, Install the Workflows app and MC1540351; generic templates require connections but none lists this template's connectors.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented the account this specific template uses for its connections.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams user is added to tag workflow connection account removal private channels. Read Create flows in Microsoft Teams and Share a cloud flow; generic connection authentication is described, but neither those pages nor MC1540351 specifies this template's connection account.

claims.claim: Any cloud-flow owner can edit its definition.
claims.quote: Any owner of a cloud flow can perform these actions: ... Edit the definition of the flow (for example, add or remove an action or condition).

claims.claim: Any cloud-flow owner can stop the flow.
claims.quote: Any owner of a cloud flow can perform these actions: ... Manage the properties of the flow (for example, start or stop the flow, add owners, or update credentials for a connection).

claims.claim: Removing an owner whose credentials a connection uses requires updating those credentials for the flow to keep running properly.
claims.quote: When you remove an owner whose credentials are used to access Power Automate services, update the credentials for those connections so that the flow continues to run properly.

claims.claim: Team owners and permitted team members can create and assign custom tags.
claims.quote: Team owners and team members (if they have permissions) can manually create and assign tags to people based on attributes, such as role, project, skill, or location.

claims.claim: The Manage tags article says Microsoft default permits both team owners and members.
claims.quote: Microsoft default is set to both team owners and members.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsTargetingPolicy reference equates MicrosoftDefault with EnabledTeamOwner.
claims.quote: Set this to MicrosoftDefault to user default setting in current Teams, which will be the same as EnabledTeamOwner.

claims.claim: In Teams for Education, non-owner students cannot manage tags when Who can manage tags is Team owners or Microsoft default.
claims.quote: If you're using Teams for Education, non-owner students can't manage tags when Who can manage tags is set to Team owners or Microsoft default.

claims.claim: Who can manage tags controls which users can manage the tags whose additions trigger the configured workflow.
claims.quote: You can change the Who can manage tags setting to specify who can manage tags, or you can turn off tags for your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: When Team owners can change who can manage tags is enabled, Who can manage tags is the per-team default and owners can change who manages tags.
claims.quote: When you turn on this setting, team owners can set whether team members can create and manage tags within a team and the value of the Who can manage tags setting is the default value for each team.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: When Team owners can change who can manage tags is disabled, Who can manage tags cannot be changed per team.
claims.quote: If you turn off this setting, the Who can manage tags setting can't be changed per team.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice does not describe what happens to channel membership when someone is removed from the tag.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams user is added to tag workflow connection account removal private channels. Read MC1540351 in full and Remove-MgBetaTeamTagMember/private-channel search excerpts; those operations do not document this template's behaviour after tag removal.

claims.claim: A tag can have up to 200 team members.

claims.claim: A team can have up to 200 tags.
claims.quote: A team can have up to 200 tags

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence statement specific to this template.
claims.quote: Searched: exact Join member to channel when user is added to tag template name with license/connectors. Read Deep dive on specific licenses, Create flows in Microsoft Teams and MC1540351; general seeded entitlements are published, but no template-specific licence statement.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a meter specific to this template.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Workflows Join member to channel when user is added to tag template licence connectors account tenant disable switch removal. Read Deep dive on specific licenses, Create flows in Microsoft Teams and MC1540351; no meter for this template is stated.

claims.claim: MC1540351 does not mention a charge.
claims.quote: No action is required. If your organization plans to use this template, we recommend reviewing your Power Automate and Workflows policies to confirm that it is permitted.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 seeded licences include entitlement to create and run cloud flows with standard connectors, without confirming sufficiency for this template's unpublished connector list.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 (formerly Office 365) / Dynamics 365 Enterprise / Dynamics 365 Professional / Dynamics 365 Team Member ... Those licenses entitle the user to create and run cloud flows with standard connectors.

claims.claim: The Workflows prerequisites section lists an account with access to Microsoft Teams and names no licence.
claims.quote:
Prerequisites
To use the Workflows app, you need an account with access to Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: The Workflows app is not available in Microsoft 365 Government tenants.
claims.quote: The Workflows app isn't available in Microsoft 365 Government tenants.

claims.claim: Workflows functionality requires the app to be enabled in Teams admin center, making app blocking a general control rather than a template-only switch.
claims.quote: The Workflows app must be enabled in the Microsoft Teams admin center in order for this functionality to work.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block controls the Workflows app's organisation-level status.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <application ID> -IsBlocked <Boolean> changes an app's tenant state.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... -Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app. ... -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant.

claims.claim: Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > policy > Edit Policy > Prebuilt connectors > connector > Move to Business classifies a connector as Business.
claims.quote: Select Security ... under Settings, select Data and privacy ... select the Data policy section ... select a policy, and then select Edit Policy ... Select the Prebuilt connectors step ... select Move to Business from the top menu bar.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorToBusinessDataGroup -PolicyName <policy name> -ConnectorName <connector name> accepts a policy name to select the policy.
claims.quote: -PolicyName: The policy name identifier. ... Add-ConnectorToBusinessDataGroup -PolicyName e25a94b2-3111-468e-9125-3d3db3938f13 -ConnectorName shared_office365users ... -ConnectorName: The connector's identifier.
claims.fix: Replace the call in controls[1].api and its rendered table cell with 'Add-ConnectorToBusinessDataGroup -PolicyName <policy ID> -ConnectorName <connector identifier>'; the reference requires identifiers, not the policy's display name.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams > Teams settings > Tagging > Who can manage tags is the route to tag-management permissions.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Microsoft Teams admin center, choose Teams > Teams settings. Under Tagging, next to Who can manage tags, select one of the following options

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks readers to review flow ownership, but the controls table has no flow-ownership control.
claims.quote: Review which teams have configured the workflow and who owns each flow. / The table lists app availability, connector data policies, tag-management permissions and the absent template-only switch.
claims.fix: Remove 'and who owns each flow' from the After rollout checklist item; flow ownership has no row in the controls table.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsTargetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ManageTagsPermissionMode <mode> updates tenant tag-management permissions.
claims.quote: -Identity: Name of the policy instance to be updated. ... -ManageTagsPermissionMode: Determine whether team users can manage tag settings in Teams. Set this to EnabledTeamOwner to only allow Teams owners to manage tag settings in current Teams.

claims.claim: The Manage tags article says PowerShell cannot manage tags, although the separately cited cmdlet reference documents tag-permission settings.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can control how tags are used across your organization in the Microsoft Teams admin center. You can't use PowerShell to manage tags.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not state whether tag-management permissions also govern who can configure this workflow template.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams tag manage tags permission configure Workflows template team owner. Read Manage tags, Set-CsTeamsTargetingPolicy and MC1540351; they describe tag-management permissions and optional team-owner setup, but no link between that permission and template configuration.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center documentation names the Teams Administrator role for using the centre.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks but we recommend using the lower privilege role where possible.

claims.claim: Creating tenant-level data policies requires the Power Platform Administrator role.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: MC1540351 recommends reviewing Power Automate and Workflows policies to confirm that the template is permitted before using it.
claims.quote: If your organization plans to use this template, we recommend reviewing your Power Automate and Workflows policies to confirm that it is permitted.
